ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the accompanying figure, inside rectangle ABCD there are three congruent circles, with centers labeled P, Q, R respectively; the three points are on the same horizontal midline, and Q is between P and R. All three circles are tangent to the top side AB and the bottom side DC of the rectangle; the circle on the left is also tangent to the left side AD, and the circle on the right is also tangent to the right side BC. The middle circle with center Q overlaps with the left and right circles, and the problem states that it passes through P and R. Reasoning: The problem gives that the circle with center Q has diameter 4, so its radius is 2. The three circles are congruent, therefore the radius of each circle is 2. Because circle Q passes through P and R, QP = 2, QR = 2. The height of the rectangle equals the diameter of a circle, namely 4. The width of the rectangle from the left side to P is one radius 2, from P to Q is 2, from Q to R is 2, and from R to the right side is one radius 2, so the width is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. Therefore the area of the rectangle is 4 × 8 = 32.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: rectangle ABCD contains three congruent horizontally arranged circles. All three circles touch the top and bottom sides of the rectangle; the left circle also touches the left side, and the right circle also touches the right side. The centers P, Q, and R lie on the same horizontal midline, with Q between P and R. From the text, the circle centered at Q has diameter 4, so every congruent circle has radius 2. Since the Q-centered circle passes through P and R, the distances QP and QR are each 2. The rectangle height is one diameter, 4. Its width is left side to P, plus PQ, plus QR, plus R to right side: 2+2+2+2=8. Therefore the area is 4×8=32.
